basics.summary: Mohsen Seyedkazemi Ardebili builds and operates AI infrastructure for Kubernetes and HPC systems in production. He designs the MLOps, observability and anomaly-detection platforms that keep large HPC and cloud-native clusters reliable - currently as UNIBO technical lead for MLOps and AI production in SEANERGYS (EuroHPC Joint Undertaking), and as the author of KubeIntellect, an LLM-orchestrated framework for end-to-end Kubernetes management, and AOBench, a benchmark for tool-using AI agents in HPC. He is a Postdoctoral Research Fellow at the Department of Electrical, Electronic, and Information Engineering (DEI), University of Bologna, has contributed to five EU projects (REGALE, DECICE, Graph-Massivizer, European PILOT, SEANERGYS), co-supervises two Ph.D. students and has co-supervised five M.Sc. theses. Before academia he accumulated over seven years of enterprise IT and network infrastructure experience, including as IT & Network Administrator at a 1,000+ MW combined-cycle power plant in Iran.

work.name: University of Bologna (DEI)
work.summary: Designs autonomous AI systems for cloud-native and HPC environments; leads AI production platform design in SEANERGYS, a EuroHPC Joint Undertaking project (Horizon Europe, call HORIZON-EUROHPC-JU-2023-ENERGY-04; EUR 32.9M, 16 partners, 2025-06 to 2029-05).
highlights: KubeIntellect — LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Framework for Kubernetes: architected a modular multi-agent system translating natural-language requests into safe, auditable Kubernetes actions across the full API surface (RBAC, exec/proxy, scaling, lifecycle, security).

KubeIntellect: LangGraph FSM supervisor with PostgreSQL checkpoints, human-in-the-loop approval on all mutating operations, and a Code-Generator agent for dynamic tool synthesis and runtime registration; FastAPI + OpenAI-compatible backend, LibreChat UI, SSH-tunnelled Kubernetes layer with RBAC enforcement and audit logging.

KubeIntellect deployed and operated on Azure AKS (Terraform, NGINX Ingress, Grafana), with the system's evaluation published in the Journal of Grid Computing (kubeintellect.com). NOTE: the paper's evaluation figures are deliberately omitted here - application documents describe capability qualitatively and never frame a paper result as a production guarantee (see projects/kubeintellect/growth/CLAIMS.md).

AOBench — First LLM Agent Benchmark for HPC Operations: 80 tasks, 5 user roles, 10 task categories, 3 difficulty tiers; 23 fidelity-validated snapshots (SLURM, Prometheus, energy APIs); Completion-under-Policy (CuP) scorer hard-fails any RBAC violation.
AOBench: evaluated 16 systems (GPT-4o to 253B open-source); best ≈45% — no system is deployment-ready (github.com/MSKazemi/aobench).

SEANERGYS (UNIBO lead): designed ExaMLOps — Prefect training pipelines, MLflow lifecycle, Ray Serve multi-model inference, Prometheus/Grafana/Loki/Tempo observability, REST + CLI (exa) + LLM natural-language control.
DECICE (UNIBO lead): led the Dynamic Digital Twin task (T2.1) — real-time modelling across device→edge→cloud→HPC with Prometheus telemetry; foundation for the project's AI Scheduler.
Anomaly detection for Tier-0 HPC (GRAAFE, ThermADNet, HazardNet): F1 up to 0.99, AUC up to 0.91; <0.2% CPU overhead at 49-rack scale (~1000 nodes).
AIOps/MLOps pipelines: Kubeflow, MLflow, Prometheus, Grafana — continuous training, deployment, and monitoring in production.

projects.name: KubeIntellect
projects.description: Operational modular LLM-orchestrated multi-agent framework for end-to-end Kubernetes management via adaptive orchestration. Domain-specialised agents (logging, metrics, configuration, security, lifecycle) coordinated by a stateful LangGraph supervisor, HITL confirmation on all mutating operations, and a Code Generator Agent that synthesises, validates, and registers novel Kubernetes tools at runtime across the full API surface (read, write, delete, exec, access control, lifecycle).
highlights: In the paper evaluation, resolved 186/200 authored Kubernetes operations queries (93% query-resolution rate).
Runtime tool synthesis succeeded on 63/77 invocations in the reported evaluation (81.8% per-synthesis success). Never call this 93% - 93% is the overall query-resolution metric.
Passed 12/16 controlled fault-injection scenarios (75%) under the reported rubric.
+25 percentage-point improvement over a tool-less GPT-4o baseline in the same paper evaluation.
Peer-reviewed in the Journal of Grid Computing (2026).
Companion CLI kube-q exposes the full agent API with HITL approval UX (https://github.com/MSKazemi/kube_q)

projects.name: AOBench (Agent Operations Benchmark for HPC) v0.2
projects.description: Trace-driven, role-aware, RBAC-enforced benchmark for evaluating LLM agents in HPC facilities. 80 tasks across five HPC user roles and ten operational task categories (Job management, Monitoring, Energy, Performance, AIOps, Security, Architecture, Data, Documentation, Facility) at three difficulty tiers, grounded in 23 fidelity-validated deterministic environment snapshots exposing SLURM, Prometheus-style telemetry, and energy APIs.
highlights: Completion-under-Policy (CuP) scorer hard-fails any run on an RBAC privilege violation
Results reported on the CLEAR five-dimension scorecard (Cost, Latency, Efficacy, Assurance, Reliability)
Evaluated 16 systems (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, 13 open-source LLMs 7B–253B, zero-tool baseline); best ≈45% completion — no system deployment-ready

projects.name: ExaMLOps (SEANERGYS)
projects.description: End-to-end MLOps platform for HPC workload management: model zoo for HPC workload prediction with auto-discovery training pipelines (Prefect), multi-stage lifecycle management (MLflow), and multi-model inference serving (Ray Serve, MinIO). Observability spans Prometheus/Grafana metrics, Loki logging, and Tempo tracing; operations exposed via a REST control plane, web dashboard with operator approval gate, an operator CLI (exa), and an LLM agent for natural-language control.
